sections.h2: How does property tax work in Boone County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Boone County property is valued by the county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), billed by the Boone County Sheriff, and taxed by several overlapping districts. The PVA sets the assessment as of January 1, and the sheriff mails and collects the bill in the fall.

Boone sits at the top of Kentucky, 256 square miles along the Ohio River across from Cincinnati. Burlington is the county seat, Florence is the largest city, and Union and Walton are the other cities. Your bill adds a state rate, a county rate, a city rate where one applies, and separate rates for the library, health department, extension office, fire district and school district. Two houses on the same street can therefore owe different totals if they fall in different districts.

Sellers should ask which year they owe. Kentucky taxes follow the January 1 owner, so a bill that shows up in September or October may carry the name of whoever held the house in January.

sections.h2: What is the Boone County collection schedule and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
For 2026 bills, the sheriff posted a discount window from October 1 through November 1, face amount from November 2 through December 31, and escalating penalties after that. KRS 134.015 supplies the pattern, so the same calendar repeats each year unless the state approves a delayed schedule.

Boone County Sheriff collection schedule posted for 2026 bills
WindowAmount due
October 1 to November 1, 2026Bill less a 2 percent discount
November 2 to December 31, 2026Face amount
January 1 to January 31, 2027Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15, 202710 percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff add-on

Source: Boone County Sheriff property tax notice.

Partial payments are refused, so each bill is settled in one payment. Card payments online add a vendor charge, and e-checks add a smaller flat charge. The sheriff's office is on Conrad Lane in Burlington, with Saturday hours in October, and bills go in the mail before the end of September.

sections.h2: What happens when a Boone County bill is still open in April?
sections.html:
A bill still open when business closes on April 15 passes from the sheriff to the County Clerk, who records a lien. The sheriff's notice lists what the clerk then adds: a 20 percent attorney fee, a 10 percent fee for the clerk, and interest of 1 percent a month. It also warns that the debt can be sold to a private buyer the following summer. For 2026 bills that transfer date is April 15, 2027.

  • Under KRS 134.015 the lien stays with the parcel for up to 11 years, whoever buys the house.
  • Warnings go to the owner of record, so a stale mailing address can hide them.
  • The Department of Revenue says the county attorney can arrange an installment plan.

A parcel with an open certificate can still be sold. The seller's share covers the payoff, and the clerk quotes it, not the sheriff.

sections.h2: What is the route to a Boone County assessment appeal?
sections.html:
Begin with the PVA. A formal appeal cannot be filed until you have met with that office, and Boone's online request form is open from October 1 to May 1. You can also email appeals@boonecountyky.org to book the meeting.

The legal window is short. Under state law the tax roll sits open for inspection for two weeks beginning in the first week of May. If the meeting does not settle the value, you file with the County Clerk by the next business day after that window ends. The Boone PVA points out that a bill itself cannot be appealed, because values must be final before rates are calculated.

  • Bring sale prices of comparable homes close to yours, the evidence the PVA's own model uses.
  • Add photos or repair estimates if the house is in worse shape than the county record shows.
  • Ask to see the sales the PVA relied on for your parcel.

The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection closes, under KRS 133.030. If you still disagree, its decision letter explains the next appeal step.

sections.h2: Why did my Boone County assessment go up?
sections.html:
Sales drive most increases. The Boone PVA values homes from nearby arm's length transactions through a computer assisted system, and every parcel gets a physical look within four years, so a jump often means several years of price growth arriving at once.

The office also points to House Bill 44, which caps growth in countywide tax revenue at 4 percent a year. That law acts on the tax rate, not the assessed value, so a rising valuation can come alongside a falling rate. Kentucky requires the PVA's values to land within 90 to 110 percent of sales prices, and a yearly ratio study tests it.

Census data shows the pressure. Boone had 135,968 residents in 2020 and an estimated 145,316 by July 2025, up 6.9 percent, across 56,021 housing units. The survey's middle owned home sits at $277,300 for 2020 to 2024, and household income of $99,414 is more than triple the figure reported for Bell County in southeast Kentucky.

sections.h2: Who gets the Boone County homestead or disability exemption?
sections.html:
A Boone homeowner who turns 65 in the tax year, or who is totally disabled, gets a flat deduction from assessed value. The PVA lists $49,100 for 2026, and the sheriff says it should print on the face of your bill once the PVA holds your form.

  • Own the house and live in it on January 1.
  • One deduction per household, even if both spouses meet the age test.
  • Disabled owners under 65 renew every year, unless the disability is a veteran's service connected rating or a permanent finding by Social Security or a state retirement system.
  • The deduction belongs to the owner. After a sale the PVA lifts it from the old address, and the buyer applies on their own.

If the amount is missing, call the PVA before you pay. KRS 132.810 allows a refund for late approval, though fixing it first is simpler. Forms go in by mail, fax, email or the PVA's online form.

sections.h2: What should a Boone County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
Closing agents commonly settle the year's tax out of the seller's funds and split it by days of ownership. The PVA notes that a bill for a house bought after January 1 may still arrive in the former owner's name, so the settlement statement is where the split gets recorded.

Three checks help. Find out whether this year's bill is paid, and ask the sheriff for a duplicate if yours never came, since that office cannot see new deeds. Make sure a recorded deed or other document updates the owner name at the PVA, because name changes happen there. For an inherited house, the PVA accepts a death certificate to update the record.

Owners with a delinquent bill, a missing exemption or deferred repairs sometimes pick a direct sale to a cash buyer, who purchases the house in its present condition, with the tax payoff deducted at closing.

sections.h2: Where are the Boone County offices?
sections.html:
Four offices cover the cycle. The PVA in Burlington values property and takes exemption and appeal requests at 859-334-2181. The sheriff collects bills at 859-334-2175, with an online portal at boonecountytax.com. The County Clerk files deeds, receives appeals and holds the bills that go delinquent in April. For 2026, the sheriff also listed Heritage Bank branches as places to pay.

Most of the county belongs to Boone County Schools, and a portion lies in the Walton-Verona Independent district, so the school share of your bill depends on the parcel. Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport is inside the county, and Census figures put 2022 transportation and warehousing receipts at about $1.87 billion.

faqs.q: What dates matter for the 2026 Boone County bill?
faqs.a: The 2 percent discount ran through November 1, 2026, and face amount through December 31. A 5 percent penalty applies in January 2027, and the 10 percent penalty plus add-on runs from February 1 to April 15, 2027.

faqs.q: Can a Boone County assessment be appealed after the bill arrives?
faqs.a: No. Appeals belong to the May inspection period. Meet with the PVA first, then file with the county clerk by the next business day after the period closes.

faqs.q: How large is the Boone County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The Boone PVA lists $49,100 for 2026. It comes off the assessment, not the bill, and applies to owners turning 65 in the tax year or totally disabled.

faqs.q: Who receives the bill if I sold my Boone County house during the year?
faqs.a: The bill goes to whoever owned on January 1. The buyer should forward it or call the sheriff for a copy, and the settlement statement divides the cost.

faqs.q: Is a Boone County home with back taxes still sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the parcel, so the unpaid amount, with any clerk and attorney fees, is normally deducted from the seller's proceeds. Ask the sheriff or the clerk for an exact payoff before you set a price.
